title: Physics Challenge
description: Test your mastery of motion, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, and classical mechanics.
seoTitle: Physics Challenge Quiz – Test Classical & Modern Physics | AI Quiz Arena
seoDescription: Challenge yourself with 10 physics questions on Newton's laws, energy conservation, optics, and speed of light.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light travels at roughly 299,792 km/s (approximately 300,000 km per second) in a complete vacuum.

questions.question: Which SI unit is used to measure electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: The Ohm (symbol: Ω) is the SI unit of electrical resistance, named after German physicist Georg Simon Ohm.

questions.question: According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, force equals mass multiplied by what?
questions.explanation: F = m * a states that force equals mass times acceleration.

questions.question: What type of energy is stored in an object due to its position in a gravitational field?
questions.explanation: Gravitational potential energy (PE = mgh) is energy stored in an object because of its elevated position.

questions.question: Which principle explains how airplanes generate aerodynamic lift through curved wings?
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's Principle states that an increase in the speed of a fluid occurs simultaneously with a decrease in static pressure.

questions.question: Absolute zero corresponds to what temperature on the Celsius scale?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero (0 Kelvin) is the theoretical temperature at which all thermal motion ceases, equivalent to -273.15°C.

questions.question: What phenomenon causes a prism to separate white light into a rainbow spectrum?
questions.explanation: Dispersion via refraction occurs because different wavelengths of light bend at slightly different angles when passing through glass.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of work and energy?
questions.explanation: The Joule (J) is the SI unit of work and energy, equal to the work done by a force of one newton over one meter.

questions.question: Which property of a wave determines its perceived pitch in sound?
questions.explanation: Frequency, measured in Hertz (Hz), corresponds directly to the pitch of acoustic sound waves.

questions.question: What is the acceleration due to Earth's gravity near the surface (standard g)?
questions.explanation: Standard acceleration due to gravity on Earth's surface is approximately 9.80665 m/s² (commonly rounded to 9.8 m/s²).
